extraction_notes: Ducommun is a Tier-2/3 aerospace structures + electronic systems sub-contractor. Filing discloses ONLY customer-level concentration (Boeing, RTX, Lockheed, Northrop, Viasat) and end-use markets (commercial aerospace, military and space, industrial). The filing names ZERO specific Pentagon Program Elements (no PE numbers, no named programs like F-35, F-18, Apache, Black Hawk, despite the cohort metadata indicating Ducommun participates in those platforms). All forward narrative is at the OEM-customer level. This itself is the J-Book divergence pattern at a meta level: a sub-tier supplier with disclosed 17.9% RTX + 5.8% Northrop + 4.2% Lockheed concentration (~28% prime-defense exposure) gives investors zero visibility into which PEs underpin that revenue. We extract OEM-prime customer-concentration claims and treat the upstream OEM platforms (F-35, AH-64 Apache, UH-60 Black Hawk, F/A-18) as the implied program exposure to verify against pentagon_jbook.

claims.claim_text: RTX Corporation (f/k/a Raytheon Technologies) generated 17.9% of 2025 net revenues and is described as a 'significant' customer, with the implication that RTX-prime defense programs (Patriot/PAC-3, Tomahawk, SM-6, AMRAAM, etc.) underpin a continuing share of Ducommun's military and space end-use market revenue.
claims.subject: RTX prime contracts (implied programs)

claims.claim_text: Boeing (now including Spirit AeroSystems' Boeing-related commercial operations as of December 8, 2025 close) generated 13.3% of 2025 revenues; commercial 737 MAX is named as 'one of our highest commercial end use market revenue platforms'. Defense Boeing exposure includes Apache (AH-64) and F/A-18 Super Hornet airframes per Ducommun's cohort metadata.
claims.subject: Boeing customer relationship — commercial (737 MAX) and defense (Apache, F/A-18)
claims.object_value: 13.3% of FY2025 net revenues; 737 MAX named as a top commercial platform
claims.source_quote: Boeing (1) 13.3 % 13.9 % 14.6 % ... Boeing was one of our largest customers in 2025, and the 737 MAX was one of our highest commercial end use market revenue platforms.

claims.claim_text: Lockheed Martin generated 4.2% of FY2025 net revenues (down from 5.3% in FY2024); LMT defense programs that imply Ducommun exposure include F-35 (named in the cohort metadata as a Ducommun platform) and Black Hawk (UH-60M via Sikorsky, a Lockheed subsidiary).
claims.subject: Lockheed Martin prime-contract exposure (F-35 + UH-60 Sikorsky)
claims.object_value: 4.2% of FY2025 revenues (declining from 5.3% in FY2024)

claims.claim_text: Northrop Grumman generated 5.8% of FY2025 net revenues (down from 6.4% in FY2024 but up from 5.5% in FY2023). Northrop accounts receivable concentration spiked to 13.3% at YE2025 vs 2.7% at YE2024 — a 5x increase that suggests a large recent shipment with delayed payment, or a single concentrated program billing event.
claims.subject: Northrop Grumman prime-contract exposure (implied B-21, Sentinel/GBSD, E-2D, JSTARS-replacement, etc.)
claims.object_value: 5.8% of FY2025 revenues; AR concentration jumped from 2.7% to 13.3% YoY

claims.claim_text: Ducommun's revenues from aerospace and defense end-use markets represented 96% of total net revenues in 2025, with backlog growing from $1,060.8M (YE2024) to $1,202.9M (YE2025), the increase primarily from military and space and commercial aerospace end-use markets. This implies forward FY26/27 deliveries against named DoD platforms — but the filing never identifies which PEs/programs comprise that military backlog.
claims.subject: Military-and-space end-use backlog growth
claims.object_value: $142.1M backlog increase (FY24→FY25); military and space + commercial aerospace end-use markets
claims.source_quote: Backlog was $1,202.9 million at December 31, 2025, compared to $1,060.8 million at December 31, 2024. The increase in backlog was primarily in the military and space and commercial aerospace end-use markets.

claims.claim_text: Ducommun's Structural Systems segment manufactures 'rotor blades on rotor wing aircraft' and 'ammunition handling systems including feed and eject chutes... for fixed-wing and rotary-wing military aircraft and military ground vehicles' — implying ongoing forward revenue from Army rotorcraft (Apache, Black Hawk) and fighter-aircraft ammunition systems (F-15, F-16, F/A-18 chain feeds).
claims.subject: Structural Systems military rotorcraft + ammunition-handling products
claims.object_value: rotor blades; M-feed/eject chutes for fixed-wing & rotary-wing military aircraft + ground vehicles
claims.source_quote: Metal and composite bonded structures and assemblies products include aircraft wing spoilers, large fuselage skins, rotor blades on rotor wing aircraft, flight control surfaces and engine nacelle components. Ammunition handling systems include feed and eject chutes, storage magazines and custom gun mounts for fixed-wing and rotary-wing military aircraft and military ground vehicles.

claims.claim_text: Forward statement: 'We expect to spend a total of $20.0 million to $24.0 million for capital expenditures in 2026... principally to support new contract awards in Electronic Systems and Structural Systems' and 'additional up-front investment in tooling will be required for newer programs which have higher engineering content.' The filing thus asserts forward contract awards justifying tooling capex but names zero specific programs.
claims.subject: FY2026 capex of $20-$24M for new contract awards
claims.object_value: new contract awards in Electronic Systems and Structural Systems (programs unnamed)
claims.source_quote: We expect to spend a total of $20.0 million to $24.0 million for capital expenditures in 2026, financed by cash generated from operations, principally to support new contract awards in Electronic Systems and Structural Systems.

claims.claim_text: Boeing-related commercial 737 MAX exposure is described as ongoing, with FAA having cleared Boeing's plan to raise 737 MAX production from 38/mo to 42/mo; Ducommun states this 'mitigates a significant portion of this risk for the time being.' This is a NON-J-Book commercial-aerospace claim, used as control.
claims.subject: Boeing 737 MAX commercial production rate (38 → 42 per month)
claims.object_value: Ducommun's largest commercial platform; FAA cleared rate increase
claims.source_quote: Boeing announced the FAA has cleared Boeing s plan to raise 737 MAX production from 38 airplanes to 42 airplanes per month.

claims.claim_text: April 2023 acquisition of BLR Aerospace — 'aerodynamic systems that enhance the productivity, performance, and safety of rotary and fixed-wing aircraft on commercial and military platforms' — integrated into Structural Systems. Used as a non-J-Book rollup-thesis control claim.
claims.subject: BLR Aerospace acquisition (April 2023)
claims.object_value: Structural Systems segment — rotary + fixed-wing aerodynamic systems
claims.source_quote: in April 2023, we acquired 100% of the outstanding equity interests of BLR Aerospace L.L.C. ( BLR ), a privately-held leading provider of aerodynamic systems that enhance the productivity, performance, and safety of rotary and fixed-wing aircraft on commercial and military platforms.

claims.claim_text: Sub-tier disclosure asymmetry meta-claim: Ducommun's 10-K names zero specific Pentagon Program Elements (no PE numbers) and zero specific named DoD programs (no F-35, no Apache, no Black Hawk, no F/A-18, no Patriot, no Tomahawk, no LRASM, etc.), despite ~28% of revenue (RTX+Lockheed+Northrop) flowing through DoD-prime channels and 96% A&D end-market exposure. This is the structural inverse of the IONQ/YSS J-Book divergence pattern — instead of overclaiming on named PEs that are unfunded, Ducommun underclaims by giving zero program-level transparency, leaving investors unable to map the defense backlog to specific J-Book lines.
claims.subject: DCO 10-K program-level transparency
claims.object_value: ZERO specific Pentagon program names or PE numbers across the entire 10-K
claims.source_quote: [Confirmed by exhaustive keyword search across 88,877-char sliced 10-K: no instances of 'F-35', 'F-18', 'F/A-18', 'AH-64', 'Apache', 'Black Hawk', 'UH-60', 'PE 0', 'Program Element', 'Tomahawk', 'Patriot', 'Sentinel', 'B-21', 'LRASM', 'JASSM', 'SM-6', 'GMLRS', 'CCA', or any analogous program designator. Only customer-level (Boeing/RTX/Lockheed/Northrop/Viasat) and end-use market level disclosure.]
